title: Enterprise residency decisional tree and price-impact model
creator: Leah Chen
description: Create a decision tree and a quantitative price-impact model that sales and legal can use when negotiating enterprise residency, retention, and subprocessor commitments. The deliverable is a short playbook (decision tree + calculator) that maps customer requirements (EU/UK SCC activation, retention window, subprocessor disclosure, private deployment demand) to a standardized set of contract options and recommended price uplift bands.
background: Enterprise prospects increasingly request bespoke residency and retention terms or require SCC activation and tighter subprocessor controls. Sales lacks a rapid heuristic to translate these asks into commercial terms. Legal performs ad-hoc risk review per deal, which slows cycles. We need a repeatable tool to reduce negotiation time and improve pricing consistency while protecting platform economics.
acceptance_criteria: Decision tree covers at least 8 common negotiation paths (e.g., hosted with SCCs, hosted + 90d retention, dedicated + on-prem KMS, VPC + subprocessor white-listing)
Price-impact model outputs clear uplift ranges (percentage or USD/month) for each node and is defensible with input assumptions
Playbook includes templated SQ answers and a curated list of required legal triggers for full review
Sales pilot of 10 deals shows time-to-Sign reduced by >= 20% or win-rate improved vs baseline
success_metrics: Median days to contract signature for pilot deals
Percent of negotiation threads resolved without legal escalation
Delta in ACV attributable to residency concessions (tracked in CRM)
Adoption: number of AE/solutions reps using the calculator in the next quarter
decision_framework_summary: Framework balances three dimensions: 1) Technical cost delta (infra/ops), 2) Compliance burden (legal review, audits), 3) Commercial risk (SLA/data residency guarantees). Each customer requirement maps to a baseline uplift band and an optional negotiation buffer. For high-impact customers we surface 'approved exceptions' that require Exec sign-off and a defined payback term.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Standardized tiers reduce customization friction but may lose some high-ACV flexibility
Overly conservative uplifts could price us out of competitive RFPs; underpricing transfers operational risk to Redwood
Estimator relies on engineering cost heuristics (GPU-hour, storage tiering) that will need periodic recalibration
implementation_notes: Build initial calculator as a Google Sheets model (v1) with clear inputs: region, retention days, SCC activation, subprocessor count, private deployment required, KMS/HSM
Parallel work: ENG to provide cost deltas for dedicated vs hosted and on-prem packaging (dependency ENG-22418)
Legal to produce templated SQ answers and a red-flag checklist for escalations
Integrate final calculator into Sales playbook Confluence page and embed a link in CRM opportunity template
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: internal discovery with Sales + Legal; collect 15 historical deals for calibration
Week 3: build v1 sheet + decision tree diagram; review with Legal and Eng
Week 4-5: pilot with 10 active enterprise opportunities; collect feedback
Week 6: refine uplifts and publish playbook; train Sales and Solutions Engineering; track pilot metrics
